notes:
Passed on the fake backend with `python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/iherrbenza__ad9959_python --backend fake` (all gates G1-G9 pass, no warnings; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null, no hardware was attached, and no hardware run is claimed. This driver is R1, so the loader does not add the R2/R3 reviewed_by gate to its hardware backend; the operator decides when to use it. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names helper PythonObjectDriver, but its one-value-per-parameter writes cannot express the upstream setter signature set_frequency(ch, freq, send) and the class needs no bridge grammar; this is a direct Driver over DDS_ESP32_lab.DDS_ESP32:DDS_ESP32 with native.py. The card's DDS_ESP32_lab.labscript_devices:DDS_ESP32 entry needs labscript and is not used. NOT COVERED: the 2-level modulation setters set_2mod_frequency/set_2mod_amplitude/set_2mod_phase, the ramp_* methods, the memory list (memory_storage/list_*), and direct_spi; raw direct_spi text would bypass every limit. The upstream class has no register getter and the ESP32 protocol sends commands without a reply, so the package declares no @read: the resource state is the last value the runtime wrote, which is the last value the driver sent, not a measurement of the output. The frequency limit is operator_required because max=clock x PLL depends on the constructor's clock and pll options; site-limits.example.json shows an example overlay (1 kHz to 100 MHz, example data only, not a fact about any board). The fake stores test placeholders and answers no real transport.
